plan.flow:
Sign-in begins at S-1. Google OAuth returns through a server-side callback; after verification, employees use the employee shell and Parking Administrators use the administrator shell. Employees with a dedicated space manage it in S-2 and S-3; eligible employees claim in S-4; employees without a registered plate must add one in S-5 before parking operations. Administrators manage profiles in S-6 and S-7, monitor weekly utilization in S-8, review entrance attempts in S-9, and configure parking and roles in S-10. Every screen is the same responsive web app at phone, tablet, and desktop widths; narrow layouts use touch-sized controls and never a native-app frame.

DESIGN.md / shared design direction: redraw every page in one consistent light interface, with a shared header per user type, one type scale, one restrained accent selected by the design system, compact tables, hairline dividers, clear status labels, and orderly HR-style people lists. Use developer-tool density for logs and reporting: plain bars, compact filters, sortable tables, and one headline metric with context above data. Use real employee and vehicle photographs where requested below. Constrain content to a centered max-width; use CSS Grid rather than percentage math; keep every item in its own non-overlapping zone. NEVER DO: emojis; Inter; generic serif fonts such as Times New Roman, Georgia, or Garamond; pure black; neon or outer-glow shadows; oversaturated accents; excessive gradient text; custom cursors; overlapping or absolutely stacked content; three equal-column cards; generic names; fake round-number metrics; AI clichés such as “Elevate,” “Seamless,” “Unleash,” or “Next-Gen”; filler scroll text or bouncing chevrons; broken Unsplash links; centered high-variance heroes. NEVER use a marketing hero, a row of three equal cards, icon-in-rounded-square feature cards, logo strips, generic KPI cards with sparklines, bento tiles, glass surfaces, or repeated uniform section templates. Replace them with a left-aligned page heading, one contextual headline measure, dense lists or tables, real product/vehicle crops where relevant, and varied but orderly section rhythm. Do not add pricing, testimonials, a marketing footer, version chips, system labels, or fields/devices absent from the requirements and sample data. The same user type sees the same menu labels and order on every page in its shell.

screens.title: Sign in
states: OAuth return with an inactive or non-Folio3 account: show a plain access message and a single “Try again” control; do not create a session.
OAuth verification failure: keep the user signed out and show a brief retry message.
screens.prompt: Draw the Folio3 Parking sign-in page alone, as a finished responsive web page in the shared light product look. Keep the content left-aligned in a narrow column with generous empty space around it, not a centered hero: first the exact page heading “Sign in” at the largest type on the page, then one sentence, “Use your Folio3 Google account to manage parking,” then the sole primary action “Continue with Google.” Below it, use one quiet line explaining that access is for active Folio3 employees. Show the Folio3 Parking wordmark with a small square P mark; no unrelated illustration, extra sign-in fields, version chip, or decorative card grid. The Google return creates a session only after the server validates the Google token, OAuth state, and active Folio3 account; do not imply a signed-in state before that succeeds. At phone, tablet, and desktop widths keep the same simple page and touch-sized action, with no device mockup.

If today has already been claimed or released, remove the release action and show the resulting status without offering a second release.
For an employee without a dedicated assignment, show “No dedicated space assigned” and the menu’s “Free spaces” destination rather than release controls.

Include a genuine photograph of Maya Chen (reuse the same person-specific portrait wherever her profile appears) and a genuine photograph of her Ford Escape at the Folio3 San Francisco office, with the plate readable; never substitute an icon or blank image. Beneath it, show upcoming release dates as a short list: 15 May 2025 and 21 May 2025, both Scheduled, and the text link “Set release dates.” Keep the rest of the page intentionally quiet. Use a compact single-column stack on phone and a restrained two-region layout on wide screens. Use this exact shared header: The Folio3 Parking wordmark sits at far left beside a small square brand mark carrying a white “P”; the employee menu sits beside the wordmark and contains My space, Free spaces, My vehicles, in that order. Parking capacity is Floor 2: 12 spaces; Floor 3: 16 spaces; Floor 4: 10 spaces; total capacity 38. Space labels used here are P2-08 on Floor 2 and P3-06 on Floor 3.

noScreen.reason: OAuth token signature, issuer, audience, state validation and authenticated-session creation happen in the server-side callback; S-1 is the user-facing sign-in and failure surface, not a separate callback page.

The initial bootstrap designation is supplied by deployment configuration, not a user-facing page. S-10 shows its completed status and provides the requested ongoing administrator settings and role assignments.
The fixed-template notification is an outbound email sent when an allocation becomes claimable; it has no page of its own.
Preserving the separate permanent-sticker process and existing temporary claims during capacity overage is an integration/business rule, not a user-facing page.

Trusted-equipment authentication, unique request ID or nonce enforcement, replay rejection, plate authorization, and the hardware indicator command are server-side LPR integration behavior. S-9 displays the resulting attempt records.
The explicit command to set the green indicator inactive and deny temporary-process entry is issued by the LPR integration on verification failure; S-9 displays those outcomes.
Daily utilization-event creation from registered-vehicle entry records is automatic backend processing; S-8 presents the resulting records and report.
Filtering the configured recipient list to Parking Administrators and sending employee-identifying weekly report emails is outbound email delivery, not a separate screen; S-10 manages the named list.
Retention follows Folio3's existing records-retention policy automatically and is not configured on a new page; S-8 and S-9 identify that policy for the records shown.

system.digest: Use 8px corners on panels, fields, buttons, and menus. Edge panels with a 1px rule and no shadow. Keep a 4px spacing rhythm, with 16px between related elements, 24px between work sections, and 40px at major breaks. Set main headings to 28px/600, section headings to 20px/600, and subheads to 16px/600. Use 14px body text with 22px line height. Make table rows 44px high and divide them with 1px horizontal rules. Primary buttons are solid and 44px high; secondary buttons are outlined and 44px; fields are white, rule-edged, and at least 44px high. Show statuses as readable words with distinct restrained status-colored text and matching fine outlines. Crop natural photographs consistently to 4:3, keeping people or vehicles legible and repeating each person's same photograph wherever shown. Give data views compact 44px records followed by a deliberate 20px pause before each distinct list section, creating a paper-ledger cadence without decorative marks.

motion.signature: Parking record settle: when a filtered record list changes, rows fade in while rising 8px over 160ms with cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
motion.ambient: While an entry check is actively resolving, its status dot breathes between 0.96 and 1 opacity on an 8s cycle using cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1).

basis.took: White employee worklists and restrained color for actions.
Formal, readable records and clear transaction status handling.
Compact scan-first tables and a single action color.
